labelled_by: Hand-labelled ground truth for the eval harness. Quotes are verbatim substrings of the transcripts.

pain_points.label: Chasing late payments is stressful and awkward

quotes.quote: I hate chasing people for money. It feels like I'm begging for something I already earned.
Chasing late invoices eats a couple of hours every month, and it's the part of the job I dread most.
I've had to chase one client for six weeks and I ended up texting the CEO directly, which felt awful.
I have to chase almost every single one, and some I just give up on

pain_points.label: Late payments make cash flow unpredictable

quotes.quote: I had to dip into my savings to pay rent.
That gap is what kills me, the cash flow, not the total amount.
That's two months of my living costs just sitting there.
I've had my card declined at the supermarket while clients owed me 2,000 euros.

pain_points.label: Hard to keep track of who owes what

quotes.quote: Half the time I forget to update it, so I'm never fully sure who owes me what.
I've definitely forgotten to follow up on an invoice before and only noticed months later.
my spreadsheet is a nightmare at tax time.
VAT rules for clients outside the country confuse me every single year.
I'm confused about whether I need to charge VAT to creators in other countries.
it's that the invoice is stuck with someone in accounts payable.

H1.why: 5 of 6 interviewees describe chasing late payments as painful; I-05 is the exception (agency payment runs).

H2.why: I-01 and I-06 would pay; I-03 and I-05 would not, I-02 and I-04 are lukewarm. Free reminders already exist.

H3.why: Everyone who discussed it says creating an invoice takes minutes with a template.

H4.why: No interview mentions cryptocurrency or alternative payment methods.

stances_note: Per-interview stance on each hypothesis with verbatim quotes. Interviews not listed did not discuss it.

H2.question: The last time a client paid late, what did you do to get paid?
H2.purpose: See what they already use for reminders and whether it worked.
H2.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.
follow_ups: What did that cost you in time?

H2.question: What tools or services have you paid for to run the admin side of your business?
H2.purpose: Learn whether and how they spend money on admin tools.
H2.bias_check: Neutral list question; the reminder idea is never mentioned.
follow_ups: How did you decide to pay for that one?

H3.question: Walk me through how you created your most recent invoice.
H3.purpose: Re-test how long invoice creation takes, step by step.
H3.bias_check: Asks for a walk-through instead of whether it is slow, which would lead the answer.

H4.question: How have your clients paid you over the last few months?
H4.purpose: Find out whether payment methods come up at all, without naming crypto.
H4.bias_check: Open question; naming cryptocurrency would plant the idea.
follow_ups: Has a client ever asked to pay another way?

PP1.question: Tell me about the last invoice you had to chase.
PP1.purpose: Understand what chasing actually involves and how often it happens.
PP1.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.
follow_ups: How long did it take to get paid?

PP2.question: How do you plan your spending when you don't know when a payment will arrive?
PP2.purpose: Measure the real effect of late payment on cash flow.
PP2.bias_check: Asks about current behaviour without assuming it is a problem.
follow_ups: When did that last cause trouble?

PP3.question: How do you keep track of who still owes you money right now?
PP3.purpose: See their current tracking system and where it breaks.
PP3.bias_check: Asks for the current method instead of whether tracking is hard.
